| [NOTE-576](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-576.md) | The Method of Characteristics Revisited: A Viability Approach | Viability is a property of a constraint set under a dynamics: K is viable if from every state some evolution stays in K, invariant if all do. Nagumo's theorem reduces viability to a tangency condition. When K is not viable, the viability kernel is the largest viable part of it, and everything else in K leaves in finite time. Stability in the Lyapunov sense is not discussed. | Read |
| [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md) | Bousquet and Slotine — Contraction and near-decomposability | Under contraction of the fast modules and of the reduced slow system, and coupling terms bounded affinely in the off-manifold state, a nearly decomposable system stays within O(ε) of its singular-perturbation reduction, uniformly in time after a transient of order (1/β_f + 1/(εβ_g)) log(1/ε), for ε below an explicit critical separation ε_c. Deterministic trajectory error only. Remark 8 prints ε_c inverted, and the slow-error bound needs an unstated d_g = 0. | Read |
| [NOTE-1466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1466.md) | Saligrama — information before commitment in safe adaptive control | A safe adaptive controller must stay safe under every model it has not ruled out. Its first action that leaves no safe continuation under an alternative is a commitment, and the evidence for it must be in hand before the action: what that action reveals comes too late. With the information gathered before commitment measured as a KL divergence between stopped records, a data-processing argument bounds any uniformly safe policy's regret below by the cost of not committing with probability ½e^{−I_pre} − α. So bounded pre-commitment information leaves a fixed fraction of the oracle gap, and a linear gap gives linear regret. Safe recovery at O(√(T log T)) is proved when a safe experiment is repeatable, informative and returns to a common state. | Read |
| [NOTE-1477](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1477.md) | Kolathaya & Ames — input-to-state safe control barrier functions | Defines input-to-state safety of a set C = {h ≥ 0}: under a bounded input disturbance d, the larger set C_d = {h + γ(‖d‖∞) ≥ 0} is forward invariant, for a class-K γ. A barrier condition with a disturbance term, ḣ ≥ −α(h) − ι(‖d‖), implies it (Theorem 1). Given an ordinary control barrier function, adding L_g hᵀ to a safeguarding controller, or the constraint term −εL_g h L_g hᵀ in a CLF–CBF quadratic program, yields such a function with ι(‖d‖) = ‖d‖²/(4ε) (Theorem 2). The enlargement is a class-K function of the disturbance bound in barrier units, quadratic in the universal construction; it is not proportional to the bound. | Read |
| [NOTE-1558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1558.md) | Liu, Zhang and Fang — Origami spring structures fitted to 3D curves | Virtual creases along the facet diagonals turn each cell of an origami spring into a one-degree-of-freedom unit, and the chain is fitted to 3D curves by optimising its folding angles: below 0.66% relative error for C, J and spiral curves with full actuation. Grouping cells to share actuators, two or three actuators fit those curves, a sinusoid needs more, and each added actuator gains less. Kinematics only; the solutions are not unique. | Read |
| [NOTE-1563](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1563.md) | Kaelbling, Littman and Cassandra — Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains | A restatement, for AI, of the operations-research theory of POMDPs that Smallwood and Sondik founded. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states updated by Bayes' rule, is a sufficient statistic, so control is an MDP over beliefs; the optimal finite-horizon value is the upper surface of one linear function per policy tree, hence piecewise-linear and convex. Information-gathering actions are valued in the same calculation as others, as the tiger problem shows. Exact solution is exponential in the worst case. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-1566](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1566.md) | Ratliff, Dong, Sekar and Fiez — A perspective on incentive design | A perspective, not a results paper. Incentive design is set on one principal–agent template and reviewed in economics (static, model-based screening and moral-hazard contracts), control theory (reverse Stackelberg games with dynamics and adaptive estimation) and online learning (regret bounds under i.i.d. or stationary agents). Each handles part of the problem; designing incentives for returning agents whose behaviour evolves with the principal's own actions is named open, with bounded rationality, information design, fairness, competing principals and counterfactual evaluation as further directions. | Read |

| [NOTE-1578](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1578.md) | Asano — Stability principle of the passive rimless wheel | For a passive rimless wheel on a slope the kinetic energy before impact obeys K⁻ᵢ₊₁ = εK⁻ᵢ + ΔE, with impact loss ε = cos²α and restored energy ΔE both fixed by geometry and slope, so the gait converges to one period-1 cycle. Linearised, the return map's eigenvalue is cos²α, independent of the step period, and the gait exists only above a minimum slope. | Read |
| [NOTE-1586](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1586.md) | Obayashi, Aoi, Tsuchiya and Kokubu — The basin of attraction of passive dynamic walking | In the simplest passive walking model, the states that take at least one step form a long thin domain, and its pull-backs under the step map nest down to a basin of attraction that is very small, thin, V-shaped and fractal-like. The authors trace this to the saddle-centre upright equilibrium: near its stable manifold the pull-backs are thinned, and non-uniform deformation folds them. Past a slope of about 0.019 the attractor is destroyed by a boundary crisis. | Read |
| [NOTE-1596](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1596.md) | Hopkins — Flexure motion stages via Freedom, Actuation and Constraint Topologies (PhD thesis) | Extends FACT from parallel to serial flexures and from kinematics to actuation. With constraints of any pitch there are 50 freedom/constraint space types; only those inside a "parallel pyramid" can be built in parallel, and the rest need modules stacked in series, whose freedoms add. A serial system whose intermediate bodies keep freedoms is underconstrained and has poor dynamics. A twist–wrench stiffness matrix gives the actuation space, where linear actuators must act to drive the freedoms without parasitic error; it depends on the flexures' geometry and material, not on the freedom space alone. One experiment located the least-error actuator line near the predicted one. | Skimmed |

Applied to monohedral quadrilateral tessellations: the Miura-ori and Chicken Wire patterns, too symmetric and so with too many modes, are not uniquely self-foldable; generic tilings rotationally symmetric about the midpoints of the tile's sides have two modes and are. | [NOTE-1622](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1622.md) | Murray and Sastry — Steering nonholonomic systems with sinusoids | A driftless system ẋ = Σ gᵢ(x)uᵢ whose velocity constraints do not integrate can still reach every configuration when the input fields and their iterated Lie brackets span every direction (Chow's theorem); a bracket is the net motion left by a small loop of inputs. Sinusoids at integrally related frequencies steer first-order, second-order and chained systems one bracket level at a time; they cannot isolate some directions of a general fourth-order system.
